prompt: Write a recorded statement transcript (about 250 words) between an insurance adjuster (lines start with 'Q:') and the claimant (lines start with 'A:'). The claimant was the driver in a low-speed head-on collision in Katy, Texas, and has back strain. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1122; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Thank you for agreeing to give this recorded statement. Please state your full name for the record.
A: I'd rather just keep it to what happened, if that's okay.
Q: That's fine. We'll keep identifying details to a minimum. Can you tell me where the accident took place?
A: It was on a two-lane road in Katy, Texas, near a shopping center entrance.
Q: What time of day was it?
A: Late afternoon, maybe around rush hour. Traffic was slow.
Q: Walk me through what you were doing right before the impact.
A: I was driving west and slowing for a turn. The other car came over into my lane. I hit my brakes, but we still ended up touching front to front.
Q: How fast were you traveling?
A: Not fast at all. Maybe fifteen or twenty miles an hour. It was more of a bump than a crash.
Q: Did your airbags deploy?
A: No, they didn't. The seatbelt locked up and I felt it across my chest and shoulder.
Q: Were you taken for medical care?
A: A paramedic checked me at the scene, and I went to an urgent care clinic later that evening.
Q: Where are you experiencing symptoms now?
A: My lower back is stiff and sore, especially when I get up from a chair. Sometimes it radiates a little into my hip.
Q: Have you had any prior problems with your back?
A: Nothing serious. I had some stiffness years ago after lifting boxes, but it went away with stretching.
Q: Are you currently seeing a doctor or receiving treatment?
A: Yes, I have a follow-up with my primary care physician next week and I'm doing physical therapy twice a week.
Q: Is there anything else you'd like to add?
A: Only that I want to get back to normal and I'm cooperating with whatever you need.
Q: Thank you. That concludes the statement.
